title: What If Lionfish Took Over the Atlantic? A Few Aquarium Fish Did

scenes.text: What if one venomous fish took over a whole ocean? In the Atlantic, it already has.
Lionfish come from the Pacific and Indian Oceans. They were first spotted off Florida in 1985.
Nothing in the Atlantic hunts them, because their spines are venomous. They spawn every few days.
On Bahamas reefs, small prey fish dropped about 65 percent in just two years.
Larger fish like snapper and grouper fell more than 40 percent, because lionfish took their food.
Now they spread from New York to Venezuela. Scientists can clear single reefs, but not the ocean.
